name: single_adaptive
fixtures: All supplied examples and tests are explicitly fictional.

interface.input: UTF-8 JSON object with user, steps, optional progress and fixture_label. Unknown fields and duplicate JSON keys are rejected.
interface.user: Required skill: novice/intermediate/advanced; required experience_years: finite nonnegative number. Optional preferences and accessibility objects.
interface.preferences: pace: self_paced/short_sessions/intensive; detail: auto/guided/standard/concise; preferred_formats: ordered unique strings; skip_optional: boolean. Preferences are soft; accessibility takes priority.
interface.accessibility: needs, forbidden_features, avoid_formats: unique string arrays. needs and forbidden_features must not overlap.
interface.steps: Unique nonempty id and title; prerequisites: unique known IDs. required defaults to not optional; optional defaults false. Nonrequired steps must be optional or have nonempty redundant_if. formats defaults to text. accessibility_support and accessibility_conflicts are step-level declarations. Optional min_skill, min_experience_years and wording_options.
interface.redundancy: redundant_if accepts min_skill and/or min_experience_years, combined with AND. Required steps cannot be skipped. Every retained step protects its full unfinished prerequisite closure.
interface.progress: completed: unique known step IDs, closed over prerequisites. Completed steps are trusted and not replanned or reassessed.
interface.output: JSON with eligible_step_ids, prerequisite-ordered plan, blocked reasons, skipped reasons, completed_step_ids and required_plan_feasible. Waiting planned steps have waiting_for IDs. Blocked descendants identify immediate blocked prerequisites; their root causes are available in blocked entries.
interface.errors: CLI emits a JSON error object and exit code 2 for validation and file errors; success exits 0. No files are changed by the CLI.
interface.callback: Python API adapt(data, wording_callback=None). Callback receives isolated planned IDs, source conditions and allowed_wordings. Must return the same IDs in the same order with exactly id, conditions, wording; conditions must be unchanged and wording must be an exact source-approved option. Invalid callback output fails closed. CLI does not load callbacks.

reference_implementation_limits: Deterministic declared-rule planning, not a trained recommender or production onboarding service.
No account persistence, authentication, concurrent updates, telemetry, network access or built-in LLM provider.
JSON input supplies all progress and facts. Skill, experience, completion, accessibility support and redundancy are trusted declarations rather than independently assessed.
Instructional detail and pacing are metadata, not generated lessons, timing guarantees or learning-effectiveness claims.
Accessibility is checked at step level, not per format; authors must accurately declare support across offered formats. forbidden_features conservatively excludes steps declaring those features.
Skill and experience thresholds are static; planned steps do not implicitly increase either value. Update input explicitly after assessment.
Blocked steps remain obligations, not skipped work; required_plan_feasible only reports whether required steps are currently plannable under static constraints.

Callback wording is constrained to authored alternatives; arbitrary generated language cannot be verified for source support by this reference. Injected callbacks are trusted executable Python and are not sandboxed.

Stable topological ordering uses input order within ready groups; no optimization of total completion time or learning outcomes. Ordering has quadratic worst-case runtime and no explicit input-size quota.
The CLI accepts one JSON file, prints a result and exits; no interactive workflow or output-file persistence.
